content:
We have mass spec m/z 224.1201 (intensity 100). That likely is molecular ion [M]+? For organic molecules, m/z 224 corresponds to formula C16H16O (exact mass: C16=192, H16=16.1256, O=15.9949 total 224.1205). Indeed matches. So formula C16H16O.

IR shows strong 1723 cm-1 (C=O carbonyl). Also aromatic region 1600s. So likely a ketone attached to aromatic ring.

Proton NMR: signals: 2.23 (s, 3H) likely acetyl methyl (CH3-CO-). 2.81 (t, 2H) and 2.98 (t, 2H) likely CH2-CH2 adjacent to carbonyl and aromatic. Aromatic: 7.17 (ddd, 7H) and 7.90 (ddd, 2H). That's total aromatic protons 9? Wait 7H +2H =9 aromatic protons. That suggests two phenyl rings, one substituted (maybe biphenyl). Total aromatic protons 9 suggests one phenyl unsubstituted (5 H) plus another phenyl with 4 H (para-substituted?). But 9 total is odd.

Let's think: biphenyl with one phenyl attached to carbonyl side chain? The SMILES we tried: CC(=O)CCc1ccc(-c2ccccc2)cc1. That is phenyl-phenyl-CH2-CH2-COCH3? Actually structure: acetyl-CH2-CH2- attached to phenyl which is para-substituted with phenyl. That gives aromatic protons: phenyl ring attached to side chain is monosubstituted (4 protons? Actually phenyl attached to side chain and to other phenyl at para? Wait -c2ccccc2 is phenyl attached at para position of first phenyl. So first phenyl has two substituents (side chain at position 1, phenyl at para). That leaves 4 aromatic protons on that ring (positions ortho/meta). The second phenyl is monosubstituted (attached to first phenyl) giving 5 protons. Total 9 aromatic protons, matches NMR.

The aromatic signals: 7.90 (ddd, 2H) likely ortho protons of the first phenyl (adjacent to side chain and phenyl). 7.17 (ddd, 7H) includes 5 from second phenyl plus 2 meta/para? But chemical shift pattern plausible.

Thus SMILES seems plausible.

Check formula: C16H16O matches.

Now we should validate with NMR simulation maybe. Use simulate_spectra to compare? Could but not needed. The task: determine SMILES using minimal analysis. We have candidate.

We should also validate SMILES with validate_smiles.
